edition: 2017 Trust Services Criteria (TSP Section 100), with 2022 revised points of focus

Security.description: Protection of information and systems against unauthorized access. The Common Criteria apply to every SOC 2 engagement.

Availability.description: Information and systems are available for operation and use as committed or agreed.

Processing Integrity.description: System processing is complete, valid, accurate, timely, and authorized.

Confidentiality.description: Information designated as confidential is protected as committed or agreed.

Privacy.description: Personal information is collected, used, retained, disclosed, and disposed of as committed and in line with privacy objectives.

notes: Security (Common Criteria) is mandatory for every SOC 2 engagement.
Availability, Processing Integrity, Confidentiality, and Privacy are included only when the entity commits to them in the engagement scope.
Type I reports assess control design at a point in time; Type II reports assess operating effectiveness over a period, typically 3 to 12 months.
Summaries and evidence suggestions are original plain-English guidance, not AICPA text. This dataset is a readiness aid, not an audit opinion.

criteria.title: Integrity and ethical values
criteria.summary: Leadership sets the tone: the company defines and demonstrates integrity and ethical values, and holds people to them.

criteria.title: Independent board oversight
criteria.summary: Whoever governs the company (board, owners, advisors) oversees controls independently from day-to-day management.
typical_evidence: Meeting minutes showing oversight of security

criteria.title: Structure, reporting lines, and responsibilities
criteria.summary: The org chart is real: structures, reporting lines, and who owns which controls are defined, assigned, and kept current.

criteria.title: Commitment to competence
criteria.summary: The company hires, trains, and retains people competent for their control responsibilities, including security training.

criteria.title: Accountability for controls
criteria.summary: People are held accountable for their control responsibilities, with consequences when controls fail.

criteria.title: Internal communication of control responsibilities
criteria.summary: Control objectives and responsibilities are communicated internally so everyone knows what is expected of them.
typical_evidence: All-hands or onboarding decks covering security

criteria.title: External communication with customers and partners
criteria.summary: The company communicates system operation, commitments, and relevant control info to customers and business partners.
typical_evidence: M SA or DPA security exhibits

criteria.title: Communication with regulators and authorities
criteria.summary: The company knows which regulators and authorities matter and communicates with them as required, including breach notification duties.
typical_evidence: Records of past notifications, if any

criteria.title: Defined objectives for risk identification
criteria.summary: Objectives are specific enough that risks to meeting them can actually be identified.

criteria.title: Risk identification and analysis
criteria.summary: The company identifies and analyzes risks to achieving its objectives, and decides how to manage them.

criteria.title: Fraud risk assessment
criteria.summary: Fraud gets its own look: incentives, pressures, and opportunities for fraud are assessed explicitly.

criteria.title: Assessment of significant changes
criteria.summary: Big changes (new product, new vendor, new infrastructure, leadership change) trigger a fresh risk look.

criteria.title: Ongoing and separate control evaluations
criteria.summary: Controls are checked both continuously (monitoring) and periodically (separate evaluations like internal audits or pen tests).

criteria.title: Evaluation and communication of deficiencies
criteria.summary: Control failures and gaps are identified, rated by severity, reported to the right people, and fixed on a timeline.

criteria.title: Control activities that mitigate risk
criteria.summary: Control activities are chosen and built to actually mitigate the risks identified, not just check a box.
typical_evidence: Control matrix mapping risks to controls

criteria.title: Technology general controls
criteria.summary: IT general controls cover the tech stack: access, changes, operations, and data backup for the systems that matter.

criteria.title: Policies deployed through procedures
criteria.summary: Policies are not shelfware: they are deployed through real procedures, assigned owners, and followed in practice.

criteria.title: System boundaries protected against unauthorized access
criteria.summary: The logical boundary of the system is defined and defended: firewalls, network segmentation, and edge controls keep outsiders out.

criteria.title: Registration and authorization of new users
criteria.summary: New users, both employees and external, are registered and their access authorized before they get in.

criteria.title: Timely removal of access for departing users
criteria.summary: When people leave or change roles, their access is removed or adjusted promptly, not whenever someone remembers.
typical_evidence: Periodic access review showing leavers removed

criteria.title: Physical access restrictions
criteria.summary: Physical access to facilities, data centers, and server rooms is restricted to authorized people.
typical_evidence: Data center SOC 2 report or attestation

criteria.title: Protection against unauthorized asset disposal
criteria.summary: Hardware and media leaving the company are tracked and sanitized so data does not walk out the door.

criteria.title: Role-based logical access and least privilege
criteria.summary: Access follows roles and least privilege: people get the minimum access their job needs, enforced by the system.

criteria.title: Controls over data transmission and portable media
criteria.summary: Data in transit is protected (encryption), and movement of data onto portable media or outside the boundary is restricted.

criteria.title: Prevention of unauthorized software
criteria.summary: Only approved software runs in the environment: unauthorized software is prevented or detected.

criteria.title: Vulnerability identification and remediation
criteria.summary: Vulnerabilities are found (scanning, threat intel) and fixed on a risk-based timeline.

criteria.title: Monitoring of system components
criteria.summary: Infrastructure and software are monitored for anomalies: uptime, performance, and security signals.

criteria.title: Security event triage and evaluation
criteria.summary: Anomalies get triaged: the company evaluates whether something is a real security event and how bad it is.

criteria.title: Incident response
criteria.summary: When a security event becomes an incident, the response plan kicks in: contain, eradicate, recover, learn.
typical_evidence: Past incident reports with lessons learned

criteria.title: Corrective actions from monitoring
criteria.summary: Monitoring findings turn into fixes: corrective actions are identified, tracked, and verified.

criteria.title: Controlled change management process
criteria.summary: Changes to infrastructure, software, and procedures go through a controlled process: request, test, approve, implement, review.

criteria.title: Business disruption risk mitigation
criteria.summary: Risks of business disruption are identified and mitigated: continuity and disaster recovery are planned, not improvised.

criteria.title: Vendor and business partner risk management
criteria.summary: Vendors and partners with access to the system are risk-assessed, contracted with security commitments, and monitored.

criteria.title: Capacity planning and monitoring
criteria.summary: Capacity is planned and monitored so the system stays available under expected and peak demand.

criteria.title: Backup and recovery procedures
criteria.summary: Backup and recovery procedures exist and are operated so the system can be restored after a failure.

criteria.title: Recovery plan testing
criteria.summary: Recovery plans are actually tested, not just written: tests prove restore works within committed timeframes.
typical_evidence: Disaster recovery test plans and results

criteria.title: Quality information for processing objectives
criteria.summary: The company defines what good data looks like: data definitions, product specs, and quality requirements for processing.

criteria.title: Controls over system inputs
criteria.summary: Inputs are checked for completeness and accuracy before processing: bad data gets caught at the door.

criteria.title: Controls over system processing
criteria.summary: Processing itself is controlled: authorized, complete, accurate, and timely, with errors detected and corrected.

criteria.title: Controls over system outputs
criteria.summary: Outputs are complete, accurate, timely, protected, and delivered only to intended parties.

criteria.title: Controls over stored data
criteria.summary: Data at rest, inputs in queue, and outputs awaiting delivery are stored completely, accurately, and protected.

criteria.title: Identification and protection of confidential information
criteria.summary: Confidential information is identified when received or created, marked, and protected for its retention period.

criteria.title: Disposal of confidential information
criteria.summary: When retention ends, confidential information is destroyed in a way that prevents recovery.

criteria.title: Privacy notice to data subjects
criteria.summary: People are told what you collect, why, and what their rights are, in clear language, before or when you collect it.

criteria.title: Choice and consent communication
criteria.summary: Data subjects are told their choices about collection, use, and disclosure, and consent is obtained where required.

criteria.title: Collection limited to stated objectives
criteria.summary: Collection is limited to personal information needed for the stated privacy objectives, gathered fairly and lawfully.

criteria.title: Explicit consent before collecting sensitive information
criteria.summary: For sensitive personal information, explicit consent is communicated, obtained, and documented before collection.

criteria.title: Use limited to identified purposes
criteria.summary: Personal information is used only for the purposes it was collected for, unless law requires otherwise.

criteria.title: Retention consistent with objectives
criteria.summary: Personal information is kept no longer than needed for the stated purposes, and protected while retained.

criteria.title: Secure disposal of personal information
criteria.summary: When personal information is no longer needed, it is anonymized, disposed of, or destroyed so it cannot be recovered.

criteria.title: Data subject access to personal information
criteria.summary: Identified and authenticated individuals can see what personal information you hold about them and get a copy.

criteria.title: Correction of personal information on request
criteria.summary: People can correct their personal information, corrections flow to third parties who got the bad data, and denials are explained.

criteria.title: Third-party disclosure only with consent
criteria.summary: Personal information goes to third parties only with consent, for the purposes collected, and only to parties with proper agreements.

criteria.title: Records of authorized disclosures
criteria.summary: A complete, accurate, timely record exists of every authorized disclosure of personal information.

criteria.title: Records of unauthorized disclosures and breaches
criteria.summary: Detected or reported unauthorized disclosures, including breaches, are recorded completely, accurately, and promptly.

criteria.title: Vendor privacy commitments and compliance checks
criteria.summary: Vendors with access to personal information sign privacy commitments, and their compliance is checked periodically with corrective action when needed.

criteria.title: Vendor breach notification commitments
criteria.summary: Vendors commit to notify you of actual or suspected unauthorized disclosures, and those notifications reach the right people fast.

criteria.title: Breach notification to data subjects and regulators
criteria.summary: Breaches and incidents are notified to affected people, regulators, and others as required, through an established process.

criteria.title: Accounting of disclosures on request
criteria.summary: On request, data subjects get an accounting of the personal information held about them and who it was disclosed to.

criteria.title: Accuracy and completeness of personal information
criteria.summary: Personal information collected and kept is accurate, up to date, complete, and relevant for its purpose.

criteria.title: Privacy inquiry and complaint handling
criteria.summary: There is a real process for privacy questions, complaints, and disputes: intake, resolution, communication, and monitoring for repeat issues.
